title: Google Gemini decouples chat history from AI training
content:
We’re updating controls in the Gemini app.
We’re giving you more control over when your Gemini chat history is used to train generative AI models. New settings let you keep your Gemini chat history, while opting out of generative AI model training. With this update, you’ll still be able to change how long history is saved and review or delete history manually at any time.
We’re also making a change to help make Gemini safer. As AI systems get smarter, we're continuing to invest in safety and security measures to help protect our users and Gemini. Now, if you turn your new History setting off, future chats will be saved for around two months; they’re used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public.
We’ll start rolling out these changes globally in the Gemini app in the coming weeks. Learn more here.

report.summary: Google now lets Gemini users keep chat history while opting out of using those chats to train future generative AI models, rolling out globally.
report.background: Generative AI assistants like Gemini depend on large conversation datasets to improve models, but using personal chats for training has raised privacy and trust concerns. Users increasingly want to retain useful conversation history without automatically donating that data to model development. Regulators and competitors are also pushing AI providers to offer clearer, more granular privacy controls. Google’s update responds to that pressure by separating two previously linked ideas: saving chat history and allowing that history to train generative AI models. The change is part of a broader effort to make Gemini safer and more controllable as AI systems become more capable and face greater public scrutiny.
key_points: Gemini now separates chat history storage from AI training. Users can keep their conversation history while opting out of letting those chats train future generative AI models, giving them more granular control over personal data.

Existing retention controls remain available. Users can still change how long Gemini saves history, review saved conversations, and manually delete history at any time, according to Google’s announcement.

Turning the new History setting off changes retention. Future chats will be saved for around two months, Google says, so Gemini can respond, process feedback, and help protect Google, its users, and the public.
The changes will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks. Google frames the update as part of ongoing investments in safety and security as AI systems become more capable.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Google’s move signals that privacy controls are becoming a product differentiator, not just a compliance checkbox. Separating data retention from model training could pressure other AI providers to offer similar opt-outs and clearer defaults. For developers, it highlights the need to design consent and retention controls separately, especially for chat logs, feedback data, and safety monitoring. For regular users, the change gives more choice over personal conversations, but the practical effect depends on defaults, discoverability, and whether “off” still means roughly two months of storage. Users should check settings rather than assume chats are never retained.
report.tools: Readers can review Gemini app data controls and Google My Activity to inspect retention settings. For privacy-first experimentation, consider Ollama with Open WebUI or PrivateGPT for local chat and document workflows, and compare retention policies across AI assistants before sharing sensitive information.
